transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood Channel), Marcus (Orbitus Partnerships), Priya (Orbitus Product), Evan (Orbitus Security), Nadia (Orbitus Sales Ops)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Objective: triage co-sell go-to-market for Orbitus expansion into EMEA and define pilot technical scope.
- Key themes: pricing carve, pilot benchmarks, security/KMS needs, lead routing and credits, timeline & exec alignment.

Topics detected: co-sell economics; pilot scope & benchmarks; security/compliance; routing and attribution; next steps/planning

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh quick roll call — we got, uh, Marcus, Priya, Evan, Nadia on the Orbitus side?
[00:08] Marcus: Yep that's right. Morning, afternoon, depending where you are. Excited to get into this.
[00:12] Diego: Thanks all. We'll kick off with a short GTM framing then dig into pilot and technical requirements. Hope that's fine.
[00:19] Priya: Works for us. We want to make sure the pilot maps to two seller-led accounts and one self-serve channel, ideally show predictable unit economics.
[00:28] Lina: From Redwood channel perspective, we want to agree on attribution, co-sell crediting, and joint marketing motion.
[00:34] Nadia: Also clarity on discount tiers and lead distribution.
[00:38] Samira: Great. I'll cover the co-sell pricing archetype, Diego will do the pilot/bench part, and Evan — maybe you'll jump in on security later.

[04:12] Diego: Quick tech context — Redwood runtime supports hosted, dedicated, and private VPC installs. For pilots most partners start hosted to move fast then pivot to Dedicated if they need guaranteed SLAs or Private for regulated data.
[04:30] Marcus: Our main ask — EMEA market entry. A mix of financial services and health tech accounts. For financials we need stronger data residency and audit features.
[04:40] Evan: Correct — for financial customers, KMS integration and HSM are non-negotiable. Also we need a SOC2 report and logging detail.
[04:50] Samira: Noted. We have SOC2 type II and can provide whitepaper links, and Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. I'll share the attestation but want to confirm the exact scope Evan needs.

[08:05] Priya: On product fit — Orbitus wants two flows: 1) an integrated assistant in their CRM (low-latency replies) and 2) a batch reranking pipeline for recommendations (throughput focused). How does Redwood show both?
[08:25] Diego: Those are classic latency vs throughput trade-offs. For CRM assistant we'd recommend lower-latency hosted model or a dedicated pool with small batch sizes. For reranking, a quantized model on Dedicated with batching saves cost. We'll propose concrete model variants and expected p99 numbers in the benchmark.

[11:10] Marcus: Pricing... how do we structure partner discounts and co-sell credits? We need to be able to resell, plus get credit when deals are sourced jointly.
[11:24] Samira: Our co-sell playbook typically includes partner discount tiers (15%/25%/35% depending on commit) and attribution windows. For resell we can offer a white-label billing flow or partner-managed resell with a cut. We'll send a matrix after the call.
[11:39] Nadia: Can you do partner-led billing? Some of our smaller channel sellers prefer to own invoices.
[11:44] Samira: Yes, we support partner-managed invoicing in Dedicated/Private contracts. Hosted customers can also set up partner billing via our partner org configs.

[15:00] Evan: On encryption, we have a specific requirement: keys must be customer-controlled and rotate quarterly; logs must be exportable to our SIEM. Are these supported?
[15:15] Diego: Yes — Private supports customer KMS and log forwarding. For hosted, we have KMS integrations and can provide structured audit logs, but for full control Private is best. We'll put a table in the security appendix that maps features to deployment types.

[18:40] Marcus: Competitors Pop up — we've been talking to BigCloud AI and EdgeServe; both offer simple per-endpoint pricing but their latency at scale is a bit variable. What's Redwood's differentiation here?
[18:55] Lina: Two things — predictable unit economics via Dedicated pools and smart routing (so you don't failover to expensive variants unexpectedly), and observability: token-level cost and latency dashboards.
[19:12] Priya: Also does Redwood support prefix caching and KV cache to reduce cost for repeated queries? This matters for CRM flows.
[19:22] Diego: Yes, automatic prefix/KV cache is in the runtime and can cut token costs, especially for repetitive prompts. We'll demonstrate with the benchmark payload.

[23:05] Priya: Pilot definition — what would you need from us to run a two-week pilot showing CRM latency and reranking throughput?
[23:15] Diego: For CRM flow: representative API calls (sample prompt sets), target p99 latency goal, and two seller accounts. For reranking: sample batch sizes, average sequence length, and target QPS. We'll need test data (anonymized) and clear success criteria.
[23:34] Marcus: Ok we can supply anonymized data for two accounts and a CSV with sample prompts. We'll need a short NDA addendum?
[23:43] Samira: We can attach a short pilot addendum; legal is used to this. I'll include a one-page pilot SOW in the packet.

[28:00] Nadia: About lead routing — if Orbitus sources a lead and Redwood introduces a customer, how is the crediting calculated? We need to avoid double counting.
[28:12] Samira: We'll set attribution rules: first-touch vs last-touch windows (defaults to 90 days but configurable). For co-sell we'll record lead id and match in CRM for analytics. Lina will help define the mapping.

[31:50] Evan: A technical question — can you support model quantization for the reranking workload and still maintain accuracy? We have some quality SLOs.
[31:59] Diego: Short answer: yes, with a caveat. For reranking we can apply 4-bit quantization on certain model families with minimal quality hit; we'll include model/quantization recommendations and a delta vs baseline in the benchmark report. If quality is critical we can run a canary on Dedicated with fallback to FP16.

[36:22] Marcus: Timeline — Orbitus wants EMEA pilot live before the end of Q3. Is that realistic?
[36:33] Samira: Timeline is tight but doable. If we lock pilot scope this week, set the pilot data share next week, and we run benchmarks the week after, we can be live in a 3–4 week window. So yes, before end of Q3 looks feasible.

[39:05] Priya: What about billing and legal turnaround? We typically need a 30–45 day SLA for contract review.
[39:14] Samira: Our standard pilot SOW is lightweight — legal has a dedicated partner path; 2 weeks is common if there aren't unusual clauses. For Dedicated/Private we can take longer.

[42:50] Diego: For the benchmark runbook I'll propose two scenarios: low-latency CRM (p99 target 200–400ms depending on model/sequence lengths) and high-throughput reranking (sustained QPS with batching, cost per 1000 queries estimate). We'll include steps to measure p50/p90/p99 and token cost breakdown.

[46:10] Evan: One more security nuance — we need proof of data-at-rest encryption in transit and proof that training data won't be retained; we run regressions for privacy.
[46:25] Samira: Redwood's hosted API does not use customer data to train models. We'll share our data-use policy and DPA. For on-prem/private it's fully customer-controlled.

[50:00] Marcus: Okay let's talk success criteria for scaling to a full GTM. We want 3 pilot wins in Q4 to justify a Dedicated commit.
[50:12] Lina: We recommend defining thresholds: one pilot with financial services account that meets security gating, plus two self-service accounts hitting defined unit economics. If those are met we can move to a tiered Dedicated commit.

[53:40] Priya: Who will be the main Redwood contacts during pilot?
[53:45] Samira: Diego will run the technical ops; Lina will manage the partner motion and weekly GTM syncs; I will be AE and manage commercial terms.

[56:30] Nadia: Can you share a sample joint press release or co-marketing template?
[56:37] Lina: Yes — I'll attach two templates: co-branded announcement and case study template.

[58:00] Samira: Quick recap of action items and next steps: Samira to send pricing matrix and pilot SOW; Diego to share benchmark runbook and sample payloads; Evan to send SOC2 scope questions; Orbitus to confirm accounts and test data. We'll aim to reconvene in one week for kickoff.
[58:30] Marcus: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[58:35] Priya: Thanks, talk soon.
[58:38] Diego: Thanks all.
[58:45] Samira: Bye.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-attributions and stopped words, some words auto-corrected. Links referenced: security whitepaper (link in follow-up email), pilot SOW (attached after call), benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared).
